dimensions.label: Motion adherence
evidence: I want to pick up right there and show you how Sally actually works day to day, then talk about what a next step could look like
dimensions.tip: Add a brief renewed discovery check before diving into product to confirm nothing's changed since the last call.

dimensions.label: Discovery quality
evidence: We've got about 40 caregivers across 65 clients, and half my office staff's time goes into just chasing down "did the visit happen, is everything okay"
dimensions.tip: Ask open questions about timeline, budget authority, and decision process rather than relying on prior-call recall and letting the prospect drive follow-up questions.

dimensions.label: Talk / listen balance
dimensions.tip: Aim for more listening — open with questions and let the buyer talk.

dimensions.label: Buying-signal detection & handling
evidence: I do want to see actual numbers before I get my team excited about this.
I'd want to loop in my ops manager too before we commit to anything.
dimensions.tip: Explicitly probe budget range and decision timeline instead of just noting the ops manager and moving to next steps.

dimensions.label: Objection handling
evidence: do families actually agree to have an AI calling into their home? That feels like it could freak people out.
dimensions.tip: After resolving each objection, confirm with the prospect that the concern is fully addressed before moving on.

dimensions.label: Proof-point fidelity
evidence: Agencies using this have seen close to 35% more billable hours recovered, because staff aren't burning time on manual check-in calls
dimensions.tip: Keep the 35% billable-hours stat tied to its published meaning (billable hours, not just admin time) to avoid conflating two different claims when questioned.

dimensions.label: Next-step specificity
evidence: I'll get the proposal built out this week and follow up with you next week to walk through it together, maybe with her on the line too.
dimensions.tip: Lock a specific date/time for the follow-up call rather than 'next week' to make the commitment firmer.

flags.evidence: That's office/admin time reclaimed — the coordination and QA work that used to eat your team's day.

recommendations.title: Discovery question bank for demo_close calls
recommendations.why: Rep leaned on prior-call notes instead of fresh open discovery on budget, timeline, and decision process.

recommendations.title: Billable-hours proof-point one-pager (35% stat definition)
recommendations.why: The rep's explanation of the 35% stat shifted mid-conversation and could confuse prospects on what's actually measured.

recommendations.title: Meeting-locking script/calendar tool
recommendations.why: Next step was directionally strong but lacked a firm date/time, risking follow-up slippage.

summary: The rep ran a competent product-and-value walkthrough with solid objection handling on privacy, caregiver pushback, and implementation timeline, and surfaced a relevant new signal (competitive losses at decision stage). However, discovery was thin—mostly recalled from a prior call rather than freshly probed—and the 35% billable-hours claim was presented then reframed in a way that could create confusion versus Sensi's published definition. The next step is promising but not locked to a specific date/time.
